chunks: And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “Do you know from where the dowries of women came to be four thousand dirhams?”

He said: “Indeed, Umm Ḥabībah bint Abī Sufyān was in al-Ḥabashah, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله proposed to her, so al-Najāshī gave on his behalf four thousand dirhams. From there these people adopted it. As for the original amount, it was twelve uqiyyahs and a nash.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: four thousand silver dirhams as a dowry amount
key_terms.أُمَّ حَبِيبَةَ: Umm Ḥabībah, daughter of Abī Sufyān, mentioned in the report
key_terms.أُوقِيَّةً: a unit of weight and monetary measure used for mahr
key_terms.النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آل: the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family
key_terms.النَّجَاشِيُّ: the Negus, ruler of al-Ḥabashah, who paid the dowry on the Prophet’s behalf
key_terms.الْأَصْلُ: the original or foundational standard referred to in the report
key_terms.مُهُورُ النِّسَاءِ: the dowries given to women in marriage
key_terms.نَشٌّ: an additional fractional measure completing the original dowry amount

ai.seo_question: Why did the dowries of women become four thousand dirhams according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the historical reason why a dowry amount of four thousand dirhams became known among people: it was linked to the marriage of Umm Ḥabībah in al-Ḥabashah. It also distinguishes that later practice from the original mahr standard, identified here as twelve uqiyyahs and a nash.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4654 - Hariz narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq who said:
Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said: "Do you know why the dowries of women became four thousand dirhams?"

Imam (as) said: "Indeed, Umm Habibah, the daughter of Abu Sufyan, was in Abyssinia when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) proposed to her. The Negus (the king of Abyssinia) gave four thousand dirhams on his behalf as her dowry. Since then, people have followed this practice. However, the original dowry was twelve uqiyyah and a nash."
